title: cori.data.qcew — Release Calendar
text: BLS publishes QCEW data quarterly. Starting Q4 2024 data (released June 4, 2025), County Employment Wages news release full data update published date. Prior , full data update lagged news release ~2 weeks. Key distinction: Preliminary annual averages published Q4 data (~June). Final annual averages published Q1 data following year (~August/September). latest_qcew_year() function defaults recent final annual vintage.

title: cori.data.qcew — Release Calendar
text: access preliminary annual data (available ~June Q4 release), use latest_qcew_year(preliminary = TRUE):
code: # Final annual data for year Y is released with Q1 data for year Y+1, typically in August. # If current month >= 9 (September or later), final data for current_year - 1 is available. # Otherwise, final data for current_year - 2 is the latest safe bet. if (current_month >= 9) current_year - 1L else current_year - 2L # Preliminary annual for year Y is released with Q4 data, typically in June. if (current_month >= 6) current_year - 1L else current_year - 2L

title: Introduction to cori.data.qcew
text: Bureau Labor Statistics Quarterly Census Employment Wages (QCEW) covers virtually U.S. jobs — roughly 95% employment — unemployment insurance system. Unlike surveys, QCEW near-census covered employment wages, making gold standard local labor market analysis. Data available county state level 1990 present.

title: Introduction to cori.data.qcew
text: get_* functions return tidy (long) format: geoid | year | variable | value, agg_var included variable rate share (support employment-weighted aggregation across geographies).
code: library(cori.data.qcew) # See all available variables and which functions return them get_qcew_codebook() # Total employment — county level emp <- get_employment(geography = "county", years = 2018:2023)  # Average annual pay — county level pay <- get_wage_salary(geography = "county", years = 2018:2023)  # Employment concentration (HHI) hhi <- get_employment_concentration(geography = "county", years = 2018:2023)

title: Introduction to cori.data.qcew
text: Two sector classification systems available via sector_type: "BLS" (default) — 11 NAICS super-sectors source data "CORI" — 3 custom super-sectors: Tradable Goods, Tradable Services, Local Services Note CORI counts: CORI super-sector employment counts stored directly. derive approximate counts shares, multiply value agg_var:
code: # BLS sector employment counts bls_emp <- get_sector_employment(   geography   = "county",   years       = 2018:2023,   sector_type = "BLS",   value_type  = "count" )  # BLS sector employment shares bls_share <- get_sector_employment(   geography   = "county",   years       = 2018:2023,   sector_type = "BLS",   value_type  = "share" )  # CORI super-sector employment shares cori_share <- get_sector_employment(   geography   = "county",   years       = 2018:2023,   sector_type = "CORI",   value_type  = "share" ) # Average pay by BLS sector bls_pay <- get_sector_wages(geography = "county", years = 2018:2023)  # Average pay by CORI super-sector cori_pay <- get_sector_wages(   geography   = "county",   years       = 2018:2023,   sector_type = "CORI" ) library(dplyr)  cori_share |>   mutate(approx_employment = value * agg_var)

title: Introduction to cori.data.qcew
code: # Specific counties emp <- get_employment(geoids = c("33009", "33011"), years = 2010:2023)  # Specific states pay <- get_wage_salary(geoids = c("33", "50", "23"), years = 2015:2023)

title: Introduction to cori.data.qcew
code: library(dplyr)  # Pull county-level employment county_emp <- get_employment(geography = "county", years = 2010:2023)  # Join your rural definition and compare # (rural_geoids would come from cori.data or ruraldefinitions package) county_emp |>   mutate(rural = geoid %in% rural_geoids) |>   group_by(year, rural) |>   summarize(total_employment = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

title: Introduction to cori.data.qcew
text: Functions return rates shares include agg_var column — employment weight used proper aggregation across geographies. example, compute population-weighted average pay across set counties:
code: pay <- get_wage_salary(geography = "county", years = 2023)  # Employment-weighted average pay across all counties pay |>   summarize(     weighted_avg_pay = sum(value * agg_var, na.rm = TRUE) /                        sum(agg_var, na.rm = TRUE)   )

what: Rural vs. nonrural employment since the Great Recession
title: Rural vs. Nonrural Employment Trends
text: Pull county-level annual employment years since 2007: Keep 5-digit county geoids attach rural/nonrural flag ruraldefinitions::cbsa_2023: Index employment 2007 levels within group show relative change: Quick stats recent year--year change:
code: emp_raw <- read_qcew_from_s3(   variables = "annual_avg_emplvl",   years     = 2007:2024 ) emp_co <- emp_raw |>   filter(nchar(geoid) == 5) |>   left_join(     select(cbsa_2023, geoid, is_rural),     by = "geoid"   ) chrt_dta <- emp_co |>   filter(!is.na(is_rural)) |>   group_by(is_rural, year) |>   reframe(tot_emp = sum(value)) |>   group_by(is_rural) |>   mutate(     index_value = tot_emp / tot_emp[year == 2007],     year        = as.numeric(year)   ) latest_yr <- max(chrt_dta$year)  chrt_dta |>   filter(year >= (latest_yr - 1)) |>   arrange(is_rural, year) |>   group_by(is_rural) |>   mutate(pct_change = (tot_emp - lag(tot_emp)) / lag(tot_emp)) |>   filter(year == latest_yr) |>   select(is_rural, pct_change) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #> # Groups:   is_rural [2] #>   is_rural pct_change #>   <chr>         <dbl> #> 1 Nonrural     0.0229 #> 2 Rural        0.0105 label_df <- chrt_dta |> filter(year == max(year))  chrt_dta |>   ggplot(aes(x = year, y = index_value, color = is_rural, group = is_rural)) +   annotate("rect", xmin = 2007, xmax = 2009, ymin = .9, ymax = 1.2,            fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.5) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1.5) +   geom_text_repel(     data          = label_df,     aes(label     = is_rural),     nudge_x       = 2,     direction     = "y",     hjust         = 0,     segment.color = NA,     size          = 5   ) +   scale_y_continuous(     labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),     limits = c(.9, 1.2),     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))   ) +   scale_x_continuous(     expand   = expansion(mult = c(0, 0)),     n.breaks = 5,     labels   = scales::label_number(accuracy = 1, big.mark = "")   ) +   scale_color_manual(     values = c(       "Rural"    = cori_palettes$ctg2ruralnonrural[[1]],       "Nonrural" = cori_palettes$ctg2ruralnonrural[[2]]     )   ) +   theme_cori() +   theme(     legend.position = "none",     axis.ticks.x    = element_line(color = "#d0d2ce", linewidth = .25),     plot.title      = element_text(color = cori_colors[["Dark Green"]])   ) +   labs(     title    = "A fragile recovery: Rural employment set back twice since 2007",     subtitle = "Relative change in employment since the Great Recession",     x        = NULL,     y        = NULL,     caption  = paste0(       "Source: CORI analysis of BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages.\n",       "Note: Indexed to 2007 levels. Rural = nonmetro counties per CBSA 2023 definition."     )   )

title: Rural vs. Nonrural Employment Trends
text: Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (hhi_emp) measures concentrated county’s employment across industries. Higher values mean fewer industries dominate local employment — sign economic fragility. Comparing rural nonrural counties Midwest illustrates plays within single region.
code: library(ggbeeswarm)  midwest_fips <- c("17", "18", "19", "20", "26", "27", "29", "31", "38", "39", "46", "55")  qcew <- read_qcew_from_s3(   variables = c("hhi_emp", "annual_avg_emplvl"),   years     = 2024 ) |>   filter(     nchar(geoid) == 5,     substr(geoid, 1, 2) %in% midwest_fips   )  hhi <- qcew |>   filter(variable == "hhi_emp") |>   select(geoid, hhi = value)  emp <- qcew |>   filter(variable == "annual_avg_emplvl") |>   select(geoid, employment = value)  midwest_co <- hhi |>   left_join(emp, by = "geoid") |>   left_join(select(cbsa_2023, geoid, is_rural), by = "geoid") |>   filter(!is.na(is_rural), !is.na(hhi)) midwest_co |>   ggplot(aes(     x     = hhi,     y     = is_rural,     size  = employment,     color = is_rural   )) +   geom_beeswarm(     cex      = 0.6,     groupOnX = FALSE,     alpha    = 0.4   ) +   scale_x_continuous(     labels = scales::label_comma(),     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))   ) +   scale_color_manual(     values = c(       "Rural"    = cori_palettes$ctg2ruralnonrural[[1]],       "Nonrural" = cori_palettes$ctg2ruralnonrural[[2]]     ),     guide = "none"   ) +   scale_size(     range  = c(0.5, 6),     labels = scales::label_comma(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()),     guide  = guide_legend(       title          = "Employment",       title.position = "left",       title.theme    = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8), size = 11),       label.theme    = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5),  size = 11)     )   ) +   theme_cori() +   theme(     panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),     axis.ticks.x concentrated economies",     subtitle = "Employment HHI by rural status, Midwest counties (2024)",     x        = "Employment HHI (higher = more concentrated)",     y        = NULL,     caption  = title: Access and Analyze BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages

title: Access and Analyze BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
text: default classification follows BLS QCEW supersector groupings — 11 aggregations 2-digit NAICS industries. source-level groupings published BLS. See full BLS definition: BLS QCEW Industry Supersectors Note Public Administration: BLS publishes government employment ownership codes (Federal, State, Local Government) rather NAICS industry. CORI derives public administration employment summing rows ownership Federal, State, Local Government.

title: Access and Analyze BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
text: CORI aggregates 11 BLS supersectors 3 custom super-sectors based whether industry primarily serves tradable (national/international) local demand. classification loosely derived methodology Eckert (2018), Appendix H1. Eckert, F. (2018). Growing Apart: Tradable Services Fragmentation US Economy. Job Market Paper, University Notre Dame. PDF Important limitations: CORI super-sectors available employment shares — counts. approximate sector employment counts, multiply value (share) agg_var (total employment). CORI classification opinionated aggregation. Use sector_type = "BLS" need source-level groupings want construct aggregations.

title: Get Employment by Sector — get_sector_employment
text: Returns employment counts shares broken sector. Two sector classification systems available via sector_type parameter:

title: Get Employment by Sector — get_sector_employment
code: get_sector_employment(   geography = "county",   geoids = NULL,   years = NULL,   sector_type = "BLS",   value_type = "count" )

title: Get Employment by Sector — get_sector_employment
text: geography Geographic level: "county" (default) "state". geoids Character vector FIPS codes. Use 5-digit counties, 2-digit states. provided, overrides geography row filtering. years Integer vector years return. Default NULL returns available years. sector_type Sector classification system: "BLS" (default) "CORI". See Details. value_type Value return: "count" (default, employment level) "share" (employment share total). Note: CORI support counts — sector_type = "CORI" value_type = "count", shares returned informational message. Multiply value agg_var derive approximate counts.

title: Get Employment by Sector — get_sector_employment
text: data frame columns: geoid, year, sector, variable, value, agg_var. One row per geoid × year × sector combination. Variable employment (count) emp_share (share, 0–1). agg_var total employment shares, NA counts.

title: Get Employment by Sector — get_sector_employment
text: "BLS" (default): 11 BLS NAICS super-sectors (e.g. Construction, Manufacturing, Health Care). employment counts shares available. "CORI": 3 CORI custom super-sectors — Tradable Goods, Tradable Services, Local Services. employment shares available.

title: Get Employment by Sector — get_sector_employment
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{   # BLS sectors, employment counts, all counties   sec <- get_sector_employment(geography = "county", years = 2018:2023)    # BLS employment shares   sec <- get_sector_employment(geography = "state", value_type = "share")    # CORI super-sector shares   sec <- get_sector_employment(     geography   = "county",     years       = 2018:2023,     sector_type = "CORI",     value_type  = "share"   ) } # }

title: Read processed QCEW data from S3 — read_qcew_from_s3
text: vintage Character. vintage read — e.g., "2024". Default: "latest", reads _LATEST pointer written write_qcew_processed_to_s3. variables Character vector. Variable names return. Default: NULL (variables). See get_qcew_codebook. years Integer vector. Years return. Default: NULL (years). geoids Character vector. FIPS codes filter . Accepts 5-digit county, 2-digit state, "00" national. Default: NULL (geographies). s3_bucket Character. S3 bucket name. Default: "cori.data.qcew". s3_path_prefix Character. Optional prefix matching one used write_qcew_processed_to_s3, e.g. "test/" dev uploads. Default: "" (prefix).

what: Write processed QCEW data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_qcew_processed_to_s3
title: Write processed QCEW data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_qcew_processed_to_s3
text: Processes QCEW data 1990 present CORI tidy long format writes complete snapshot S3. call creates new vintage. _LATEST pointer file also updated read_qcew_from_s3 can find current vintage automatically.

title: Write processed QCEW data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_qcew_processed_to_s3
code: write_qcew_processed_to_s3(   vintage = NULL,   years = 1990:as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")),   staging_dir = "data/qcew",   s3_bucket = "cori.data.qcew",   s3_path_prefix = "",   overwrite = FALSE,   sync_to_s3 = TRUE )

title: Write processed QCEW data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_qcew_processed_to_s3
text: vintage Character NULL. Vintage label use (e.g., "2024"). NULL (default), derived max(years). years Integer vector. Years include. Default: 1990 current year. staging_dir Character. Local staging directory BLS downloads. Default: "data/qcew". s3_bucket Character. S3 bucket name. Default: "cori.data.qcew". s3_path_prefix Character. Optional prefix S3 keys, e.g. "test/" development. Default: "" (prefix). overwrite Logical. TRUE, delete existing S3 vintage prefix uploading. Use re-publishing vintage. Default: FALSE. sync_to_s3 Logical. Upload S3 writing locally. Default: TRUE.

title: Write processed QCEW data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_qcew_processed_to_s3
text: Invisibly, named list: $vintage $n_rows.

title: Write processed QCEW data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_qcew_processed_to_s3
text: processed output contains one row per geoid/year/variable, columns geoid, year, variable, value, agg_var. See get_qcew_codebook variable definitions.

title: Write processed QCEW data to S3 as a versioned vintage — write_qcew_processed_to_s3
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Full run -- auto-names vintage from data write_qcew_processed_to_s3()  # Local only, scoped years write_qcew_processed_to_s3(   years      = 2019:2024,   sync_to_s3 = FALSE )  # Re-publish same vintage after adding data write_qcew_processed_to_s3(vintage = "2024", overwrite = TRUE) } # }
